Triage: `domain:spec` confirmed; **type `Bug`, `priority:p3`, `pm:queue`.**

**Fence independently re-verified, not taken from the card.** It was held by **#17474** — read 2026-09-10T19:30:55Z: **`closed`**, and the card's own probe re-run on current `origin/main` gives `git grep -c 'only widget type' -- packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts` = **1**, matching what the card measured. ⇒ Dispatchable.

Carriers: `dashboard.widgets` (**17**) and `dashboard.globalFilters` (**10**) in `packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts`.

⚠️ **Six `retiredKey()` tombstones are excluded from those counts** (5 on `dashboard.widgets`) and are #17502's, which this seat graded p2 earlier today. ⛔ **Do not title a tombstone** — a titled tombstone is a *better-presented* offer of a key the parse door refuses, which is worse than an untitled one.

## The family, graded as one shape

All three are `Part of #17232` (`pm:dispatched`, p2) and share the mechanism that makes them measurable — `packages/spec/src/kernel/repeater-item-titles.test.ts`, an **exact, shrink-only ledger**: a carrier absent from it must be fully titled (a new untitled repeater reds on arrival), and a carrier present in it must still be untitled (a paid debt must be **deleted** from the ledger).

⭐ That ledger is why these are p3 rather than anything worse: **the debt cannot grow.** A new untitled repeater reddens immediately; what remains is a fixed, enumerated backlog.

⇒ Each card is one carrier set = one slice = one changeset. ⛔ **Do not fold them into one dispatch**: they touch three different files, and folding gate ② (same package/area, one worktree, one changeset) fails on the file face even though the package is shared.

⚠️ Counts were derived **through the platform's own predicate** (`z.toJSONSchema` over `getMetadataTypeSchema`), ⛔ not by regexing source. Re-derive the same way; a source regex will disagree and the ledger will red.

`priority:p3`: raw property keys as column headers in the Studio property panel. Nothing behaves wrongly, no data moves, and the reader is a metadata author looking at a panel — not an end user. `type Bug`: the panel shows an identifier where the schema means to show a title.

## Round returned `done`. ⛔ Two corrections to this seat, both measured by the round, both mine.

`domain:spec` execution seat, `session_01KB5PFtxuy1x3dcR5gxudx6`, 2026-09-16T16:57Z. ⛔ No label change; card stays `pm:dispatched` with its assignee. An isolated at-tier review starts next.

### ⛔ 1. My「the card's 27 is a 2026-09-10 reading」 warning — the method was right, the inference was wrong

I told the round that `#17616` (「refuse `dashboard.widgets[].options.stageOrder` on every widget type that does not read it」) had probably moved the count, and to re-derive it.

Re-deriving was correct and it is what I asked for. **The answer is that the count did not move: still 17 + 10 = 27.** And the reason is structural, not incidental:

> `stageOrder` lives **inside `options`** — one level below the repeater's row properties, where `options` itself is the single row property — so a refusal at that depth **cannot** move this count.

⇒ ⛔ I reasoned from 「the file moved」 to 「the population moved」 without asking **at what depth**. The card's number was never stale. ⭐ The right shape of my warning was 「this is a premise to re-derive」; the wrong part was the 「⚠️ it probably changed」 I wrapped around it, which is a prediction wearing a measurement's clothes.

### ⛔ 2. My claim comment omitted the `Session:` line, and the gate says so

`check-clause2-carriers --pair 18505` → exit **0**, but it prints:

> ATTRIBUTION NOT VERIFIED: the governing claim comment carries no `Session:` line, so there is nothing to compare the correction against. The reading stands.

Advisory, ⛔ not blocking — but it is real: my `Clause-②-correction` comment carries a `Session:` line and the **claim** it corrects does not, so nothing can check they are the same session.

⚠️ And the cause is the one I already owned once today: **the template carries the line and I did not copy it.** `SKILL.md:802` spells `Session: \`session_<id>\`` immediately above the `Clause-②` line. That is now **three** claim-comment defects this shift from composing the block from memory — the malformed `Clause-②` line on #17235, the same on this card, and this omission. ⛔ Not filing a card: the template is correct and the repo is not at fault. The fix is that this seat copies `SKILL.md` 〈模板与表〉 verbatim, every time.

### What the round did that is worth naming

⭐ **It re-pointed a dark control its own change would have silently invalidated.** `dashboard.test.ts` used `widgets[].id` as the 「a sibling with no authored title has none」 control — and this change **titles** `widgets[].id`. Rather than delete the control or let it pass for the wrong reason, it re-pointed it onto a **tombstone** (`widgets[].actionUrl`) and gave it a lit leg (`widgets[].id` is now `'Widget ID'`). ⇒ the control now pins the tombstone rule instead of borrowing a coincidence. That is the 「does my test still recognise what it should not?」 question asked of its own suite.

⭐ **The ledger pin is exact in both directions**, so the run 「would have gone RED had the titles landed without the ledger deletion, or the deletion without the titles」. Measured via `--reporter=verbose`, not asserted.

**Tombstones**: exactly 5 on these two carriers, all on `dashboard.widgets`, `globalFilters` holds 0 — and all 5 still emit `title=undefined` in **both** io modes after the change. ⛔ Nothing got a title that should not: the other 20 repeater carriers hold their exact prior untitled counts (field:options 6, object:fields.options 6, view:columns 14, view:sort 2, view:tabs 9).

**Fence held**: `check:authorable-surface` green and `packages/spec/authorable-surface.base.json` neither moved nor was touched ⇒ the anchor-only PR that owns that file is unaffected.

### Two files outside the declared face — reported, ⛔ not taken silently

The LEDGER (`repeater-item-titles.test.ts`) and the `dashboard.test.ts` control above. The first is the card's own stated second half (「then remove this carrier's ledger entry」) and leaving it would be as red as never paying; the second is the re-pointing. `dashboard.form.ts` was deliberately **not** touched — enumerating repeater children is the i18n-catalog half and belongs to **#17508**. All three calls are right.

### For the successors, not this card

- The card body and its triage comment say 「Six tombstones (5 on `dashboard.widgets`)」. Re-derived: these two carriers hold exactly **5**, `globalFilters` holds 0 ⇒ the sixth is on neither carrier of this card. An attribution error in the count, ⛔ not in the work. 承接者: **#17502**.
- `check:cross-package-test-inputs` — already **#18348** (and #18440 / #18495). ⛔ Not re-filed. ⭐ But this round produced a **sharper repro than any of those cards carry**, and it is worth having on the surviving card: in a clean control worktree with **zero** source changes the gate exits 0; `mkdir -p packages/spec/dist && echo 'export {};' > packages/spec/dist/index.js` flips it to exit 1 with the identical finding; removing `dist` restores exit 0. ⇒ two lines reproduce it from nothing. This seat will carry that onto #18348.

- `git merge-base --is-ancestor 97233b90ca origin/main` → **exit 0**; the squash is main's tip.
- **Subject probe (lit):** `.meta({ title` in `packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts` → **31 occurrences** (`grep -o | wc -l`, i.e. occurrences, not lines), matching the review's measured 4 → 31.
- **Lit control, same file:** `z.enum(` → 6 occurrences, so the probe reads a file it can see.
- **Dark control:** `.meta({ zztitlezz` → **0**.
- **Ledger:** the only surviving mention of the two carriers in `packages/spec/src/kernel/repeater-item-titles.test.ts` is the prose at `:94` — "`dashboard:widgets` and `dashboard:globalFilters` were paid by #17505" — i.e. both ledger ENTRIES are gone, exactly as the review measured, while the lit control `view:columns` is still there.

At-tier contract review PASSED on head `82838f4fac` (record posted verbatim in the PR thread, tier census 103/103); both carriers were cleared in one stroke, `--pair 18505` exit 0, and the landing pre-check's three conditions were read after the last state write. `pm:dispatched` comes off here — a closed card carrying a pm state label is a half-state. `domain:spec`, `bug` and `priority:p3` stay: attribution is not state.

### Residue, filed rather than left in a comment

- **#18517** — the `dashboard.test.ts` control this PR re-points pins the untitled-tombstone rule for **1 of the 5** tombstones on the widget row, not the class. Measured by the reviewer: titling `actionUrl` reds 2 cases; titling `aria` or `actionType` passes all 109. The card carries the reviewer's verified recommended shape (iterate the `[REMOVED] `-described entries and assert `title` undefined for each, keeping the `'Widget ID'` lit leg). **Not owed by this PR** — it titles no tombstone, and #18231 strips unsatisfiable nodes from the served schema regardless of `title`.

### A seat correction, on the record

The dispatch for this round warned that #17616 had "probably moved" the count of 27. The reviewer measured **27** on today's tree in both io modes and named two independent reasons it could not have moved — `stageOrder` sits one level below the row properties, and #17616 is a `superRefine` refusal rather than a schema removal. The warning was a prediction wearing a measurement's clothes; the card's count was never stale.

⚠️ For the parent #17232: this closes the `dashboard.widgets` (17) + `dashboard.globalFilters` (10) half. The five ledger survivors remain — `field:options` 6, `object:fields.options` 6, `view:columns` 14, `view:sort` 2, `view:tabs` 9 — and are #17506's and #17507's.
